title: Exception Handling & Graceful Error Recovery
why: Tools fail frequently: network timeouts, invalid JSON responses, missing database keys. If your tool crashes with an uncaught exception, your whole agent crashes. Instead, you must catch errors and feed them back to the LLM so it can retry with new parameters.
objectives: Catch specific exceptions rather than bare except:
Convert runtime errors into informative error messages for the LLM
Implement retry loops with exponential backoff
concept: In agent design, exceptions are not fatal errors; they are observations. When a tool fails, returning 'Error: Invalid date format. Please use YYYY-MM-DD.' allows the LLM to self-correct on the next step.

practice.description:
Wrap an HTTP request function in a try-except block that handles 
equests.exceptions.ConnectionError and returns an actionable LLM prompt string.
practice.hint: Catch ConnectionError and return a message asking the agent to verify network connectivity.

requirements: Simulate flaky tool that fails 50% of the time
Implement automatic retry mechanism up to 3 times before returning observation failure

checklist: Understood why tools must return error strings instead of crashing
mistakes: Silently passing exceptions (except: pass), leaving the agent confused with None values
